subject: Token economics & startup discount — next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@draftly.ai>
Cc: James Park <james@spry.io>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up — token volumes & pricing

Hi Sofia — really enjoyed the demo today. Quick recap + next steps from my side so we can surface the right pricing paths for Draftly.

Recap of what we heard on the call:
- Expected steady production: ~25M tokens / month for core writer flows
- Marketing/demo bursts: spikes up to ~80M tokens in some months
- Primary constraint: annual budget band for infra is ~ $30k–$40k for year 1 (you mentioned seed-stage runway)
- Goal: keep unit economics around $/1M tokens that lets you iterate without surprises

A couple of clarifying asks so I can model pricing:
1) Is the 25M/month an average or a guaranteed minimum?
2) Do you expect burst months in Y1 (yes/no + rough month count)?
3) Are you interested in a committed-use price (discount in exchange for a token commitment) or do you prefer an unconditional startup program discount for year 1?

To make the conversation concrete, our baseline hosted list price for the family of models we discussed is $18 / 1M tokens. Ballpark ways we typically structure this for startups:
- Startup program: one-year promotional discount (often 50–65% off) to help product-market fit, no long-term commitment required.
- Committed-use: lower unit price in exchange for a 12–24 month token commit (tiered by total tokens).
- Multi-year incentive: 3–5% additional off when you sign a 24+ month committed contract.

If Draftly is targeting an effective target price, tell me the target $/1M you have in mind (example: $10 / 1M or $5 / 1M) and I will map to the options above and return three concrete proposals (no surprises).

Attached: draft_pricing_v1.pdf — simple worksheet I’ll fill in once I have your average vs min and commitment preference.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three clarifications above, I’ll circulate a short proposal and an example SOW. If you want to keep this high-level, I can also propose two options today (startup promo vs 12-month commit).

Thanks again — great conversation.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@draftly.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james@spry.io>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — token volumes & pricing

Hi Dylan — thanks for the recap and the worksheet. Quick answers:
1) The 25M is our expected average once we roll out 1.0 to customers; we can commit to a 10M/month minimum during pilot months.
2) We expect 3–4 burst months tied to marketing pushes; bursts push usage up to 70–80M in a month.
3) We are very interested in the startup program given stage (seed, raised $750k) but would consider a committed-use if discounts are meaningful and align with our runway.

Target price: ideally $10–12 / 1M tokens for year 1 to keep ops affordable while we grow. If you can get close to that with a startup promo + light commitment, we can move quickly.

Also — can you confirm whether startup credits stack with committed discounts or if they’re mutually exclusive? We’d prefer something that gives us immediate runway but still benefits from predictable committed pricing later.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Alvarez, Head of Product — Draftly
Attachment: draft_team_chart.png (image stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@draftly.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draftly — pricing ask / approval request

Marissa / Dev / Aditya — looping you in for approval on a startup + committed structure for Draftly. Client background: seed stage, ~25M avg tokens expected; target $10–12 / 1M. They’re asking whether startup program and committed discounts stack.

Proposal I’d like to offer (subject to signoff):
- Option A (Startup promo): 60% off hosted list for the first 12 months, no long-term commitment required. Effective rate = $7.20 / 1M tokens for year 1.
- Option B (12-month committed): Commit to 300M tokens over 12 months (25M/month average). Committed discount = 20% off list => $14.40 / 1M. If they are eligible for the startup program, we can offer a one-time onboarding credit but not stack the full startup % on top of committed discounts.
- Option C (24-month committed): Commit to 600M over 24 months => committed discount 25% + multi-year incentive 5% = 30% off list => $12.60 / 1M.

Notes / ask:
- My read: Draftly needs runway — Option A gives the best short-term runway ($7.20) and is easiest to move on. But if they want predictable unit economics while scaling, Option C is the most attractive over time.
- Do we have margin flexibility to approve Option A (60% for 12 months) for seed-stage customers, or should we cap at 50%?
- If we approve Option A, I’ll prepare a short SOW + DocuSign and get legal to add a single clause preventing stacking of discounts.

Attachments: proposed_terms_for_draftly.pdf (term sheet stub)

Can you please confirm approvals or suggest edits? I’d like to respond to Sofia today.

Thanks — Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia@draftly.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draftly — pricing ask / approval request

Dylan / team / Sofia — quick approval and framing from my side. Thanks for the clear options.

Decision: Approve Option A with a small modification and an explicit path to Option C.
- Approved: Startup program promo at 60% off list for the first 12 months (effective $7.20 / 1M tokens).
- Condition: Requires a 3-month minimum usage commitment at a 10M/month floor to avoid abuse during pilot.
- Stacking: Do not stack full startup % with committed-use discounts. Instead, offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first-year committed value if the customer later converts to a 12+ month committed contract.
- Upsell path: If Draftly signs a 24-month commit (>=600M tokens total), we’ll move them to Option C pricing (30% total committed + multi-year) for the remainder of the term.

Legal / billing: Dev — please draft the SOW with the conditional language (3-month minimum, onboarding credit clause) and prepare the DocuSign envelope. Aditya — if there are billing or quota guardrails we need on the Hosted tenant, please add them (burst protection, overage handling).

Sofia — happy to get you the final one-page offer + SOW. If that looks good, I’ll ask legal to route DocuSign this afternoon.

Best,
Marissa Cole | Sales Director, Redwood Inference
